answer: Identity aging undercuts sybils. Privileges must not bloom overnight: a new key starts as bare ivory and seasons before it can vote, vouch, or earn. Trust compounds with witnessed history, like a willow whose roots took years to anchor the riverbank; you cannot clone age, only accrue it. Each epoch survived with honest countersignatures adds weight, so a million fresh sybil keys stay weightless infants. The economy becomes a haven for the patient: months of clean attested behavior per identity makes manufactured trust costlier than any reward. Time is the one thing a botnet cannot mint.
